en: Now in this starting application I prepared
for you,
we start on that authentication screen here.
And that screen shows a form which already
got an HTMX attribute on it.
And in there I got some inputs which also
have HTMX attributes on them.
And I'm only using attributes here which you
already saw earlier in the course. To be
precise, I added those attributes so that a
POST request to /login is sent if the form
is submitted.
And in addition, I'm sending POST requests
to /validate if one of those input fields
changes.
And that's important. The POST request on
the input field will be sent when the input
changes because that's the default event to
which HTMX listens.
And an input field is treated as changed if
the user entered a value and then does
something different, for example,
moves the focus to a different input field.
In that case, this POST request to /validate
would be sent.
I then also make sure that I target this
paragraph here, which comes after the input.
So the next paragraph in line for the
response of this POST request
because this POST request, which is handled
by this route, will lead to a response that
either includes an error message
or nothing if the input is valid.
And therefore, I wanna make sure that I
either show the error message between those
paragraph tags here or nothing if there is
no error.
That's how this application works at the
moment.
As a result, if you reload here and you
enter an invalid email, for example, just
test, then you should see that an error
message is showing up here.
However, what you'll also see is that if you
enter some invalid password,
which basically means that you enter a
password that's too short,
you also get email address is invalid here
and that of course doesn't make a lot of
sense.
Now, in theory,
I prepared this validation code such
that I wanna return a password-specific
error message if the password is wrong.
But for some reason, that doesn't seem to
work and that's therefore the first thing
we'll work on.
We'll tweak the request that's being sent to
validate to make sure that we attach the
right data because as you'll see in the next
lecture, the problem we currently have,
the problem that leads to this incorrect
output is that the wrong data is sent with
those requests.
